functionality.rationale: An aggregation that diverges from agent.sh list or delivery_plan.py status would misrepresent delivery progress and mislead scheduling decisions, so the dashboard must reuse the existing state logic and be verified against it.

security.rationale: Task titles and free-form backlog text are rendered into HTML; without escaping, untrusted content could inject markup into the generated page.

performance.rationale: The generator reads a bounded set of tracked files and task branches once per run; there is no hot path or runtime cost to the shipped product.

compatibility.rationale: The change adds a new read-only subcommand and gate without altering the C ABI, wire protocol, persisted schema, or any shared cross-workstream contract.

concurrency.rationale: Generation is a single-shot read of repository state and task branches; it holds no locks and mutates no runtime state.

platform.rationale: The generator is pure Python 3 over Git and tracked files, matching the existing harness tooling, and emits a platform-independent static HTML file.

persistence.rationale: The dashboard persists nothing authoritative; its only output is a git-ignored generated HTML artifact derived entirely from the tracked sources of truth.

adr.rationale: The dashboard is a read-only, purely derived reporting tool. It introduces no new or changed public cross-workstream contract, security profile, persisted format, or architecture decision that is expensive to reverse.

architecture.rationale: No production runtime module moves and no dependency direction changes; the tool lives within the integration workstream under tool/harness.

roadmap.rationale: The dashboard reports on existing delivery progress and adds no product scope or milestone sequencing.
